title: Further coordinated frame cuts on #186: conditional κ = 6.62651985348746e-4
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Continue #186's physical-frame search with coordinated intersections and joins, including line/hyperplane proposals. The complete checked result is **κ = 331325992674373 / (5·10^17) = 0.000662651985348746**, about **0.1158% above #186**.

This changes 1,361 operation frames on #186's unchanged scalar word. All 2,310 aliases, read deadlines and 46 terminal actions remain fixed. Complex W=13,326, rank=878,196 and deficit=1,320 are unchanged; the paid complex saving rises to 0.000663091384170935. The parent's completed bank-bit supplier remains checked and sufficient.

Concurrent #193 reports a higher 0.0006647872 using a different source-assisted word; this is not a current-record claim. The contribution is a further fully replayed frame witness and open integer-capacity cut search on the #186 construction. Directed cut and #186's subspace method are credited, not claimed as new.

Stacked on #186 at `166a34d75e853e933855f0f7e940fe77c4bb6b8d`. All inherited all-size compiler, bank/shared-core, weighted-bit, restored-row, prime, precision, recovery, balanced-layout and fixed-tape interfaces remain conditional. No unconditional theorem or practical runtime improvement is claimed.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/continued-frame-cuts-186/verify.py
```

The full offline authoring run passed in 143 s. It verifies the immutable parent/source archive and its entire complex/bit certificate, then independently checks the new complex geometry, every rational source/target/dirty column in both shear directions, all 46 terminal trajectories, exact moment/successor, the full paid bridge, all 47 strict inequalities and seven margins. Corruption controls reject omitted group stock, a bad child recount, a zero frame and the next kappa grid point. No search or third-party dependency is used by verification.

`RESULTS.md` is generated from the certificate and checked on reproduction. Optional `search.py` requires numpy and writes a separate candidate; its output still requires full terminal and assembly admission. The cut solver uses Python integer capacities; its min cuts were independently compared with exhaustive cuts on 70 small graphs, including capacities above 32 bits.

The new CI runs the read-only aggregate. Original package bytes are unchanged.

## Credits

#186 / @Dugongue supplies the combined witness, subspace-cut direction, rematch and entrance-bank construction. @chafreaky supplies the shared-edge word and exact formal/terminal checks; @eumemic supplies PR168 v4 and its module/word/physical-layer lineage; @jamesyc supplies terminal accumulation and compensated birth reuse; @icekylinx and all predecessor contributors retain the full framework credit. Original manifests, notices and immutable source package remain intact.

Prepared by **huxint with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**. Apache-2.0.
